n: This verse concludes chapter 3: so many men will die in war that seven women will beg one man to marry them, not for support but to remove the shame of being unmarried and childless.

f.w: seven women shall take hold of one man

f.g: Disgrace — in Israel, being unmarried or childless was considered a deep shame.

n: After the judgment, the “branch of the Lord” will flourish in beauty and glory for the survivors of Israel. Many read the Branch as a title for the Messiah, Jesus Christ.
Those who remain in Zion and Jerusalem will be called holy — everyone whose name is recorded among the living. God keeps a record of His people.
This will happen once the Lord has washed away Zion’s moral filth and Jerusalem’s bloodguilt with a cleansing spirit of judgment and burning.

The Lord will place over every home and gathering in Zion a cloud by day and fire by night — like the pillar that guided Israel out of Egypt. His glory will be their canopy. 2 Nephi 14:5 reads “upon all the glory of Zion.”

f.w: a cloud and smoke by day

f.g: A canopy or covering, like a wedding canopy (Hebrew ḥuppah).

n: It will also be a shelter: shade from the heat and a refuge from storms. Latter-day Saints often link this with the stakes of Zion as places of defense and refuge.
